version.changelog: Initial release: Shopify order lifecycle management with 5 n8n workflows

llm.summary: The skill's workflows match its Shopify/order-management purpose, but there are implementation mismatches and security-relevant omissions (notably missing declared env vars and no webhook signature verification) that need fixing before trust.

dimensions.detail: Name/description align with the actual workflows: Shopify Admin API calls, Google Sheets logging, and SMTP emails are all required for the claimed features (new orders, status sync, low-stock alerts, abandoned-cart recovery, daily reports). n8n credentials (Google Sheets, SMTP) and Shopify API access are expected for this functionality.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The SKILL.md and included n8n workflows reference and use only Shopify, Google Sheets, and SMTP endpoints (expected). However: (1) the new-order webhook parsing node extracts the Shopify HMAC header but does not perform signature verification — SKILL.md asks you to set SHOPIFY_WEBHOOK_SECRET but the workflows do not validate it, leaving the webhook endpoint vulnerable to spoofed requests; (2) the runtime instructions and workflow JSON reference additional environment values (SHOPIFY_ORDERS_SHEET_ID, SHOPIFY_ADMIN_EMAIL, LOW_STOCK_THRESHOLD) that are not listed in the declared required envs in metadata, creating a documentation/configuration mismatch; and (3) the abandoned-cart workflow sends recovery emails directly to customer addresses (expected behavior) but this means the skill can send arbitrary outbound email to third parties once SMTP creds are provided — consider consent/anti-abuse controls.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Instruction-only skill with no install spec and no code files beyond n8n JSON workflows. Nothing is downloaded or written by an installer here, which minimizes install-time risk.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Requested/required Shopify env vars (STORE_URL, ACCESS_TOKEN, WEBHOOK_SECRET) are appropriate for Shopify API/webhook usage. n8n Google Sheets and SMTP credentials are also expected. But SKILL.md requires additional env/config (SHOPIFY_ORDERS_SHEET_ID, SHOPIFY_ADMIN_EMAIL, LOW_STOCK_THRESHOLD, and placeholder credential IDs) that are not declared in the registry metadata's required env list — this mismatch reduces transparency and may lead to misconfiguration. The number and sensitivity of credentials is proportional to the skill, but you should ensure the Shopify access token has least privilege and that SMTP creds are limited to sending only intended messages.

dimensions.detail: always is false and there's no install-time script or skill-level persistence requested. The skill will operate only when invoked by the agent (user-invocable/autonomous invocation defaults). No elevated platform-wide privileges are requested.

llm.guidance:
This skill appears to do what it says (Shopify → n8n → Sheets → email), but you should not install it without addressing the following first:

1. Webhook security: the 'Parse Order' workflow reads the Shopify HMAC header but does not validate it. Add HMAC verification using SHOPIFY_WEBHOOK_SECRET in the webhook handling node/code so only legitimate Shopify webhooks are accepted. Without this, attackers can post fake orders or trigger workflows.

2. Configuration/documentation mismatch: ensure the registry metadata's required env list includes SHOPIFY_ORDERS_SHEET_ID, SHOPIFY_ADMIN_EMAIL, and LOW_STOCK_THRESHOLD (and any other placeholders). Confirm you set these before importing the flows.

3. Principle of least privilege: create a Shopify access token scoped only to the minimum required permissions (read_orders, read_products, read_checkouts). Prefer creating a dedicated API credential (not a full admin token) and rotate it regularly.

4. SMTP risk: the skill will send emails to customers (abandoned-cart recovery) and admins. Use an SMTP account restricted to your store/domain, enable DKIM/SPF, and monitor outgoing email so it cannot be abused to send spam.

5. Test in staging: import and run the workflows in a non-production store first to validate behavior and rate limits. Confirm Google Sheets append/update behavior (matching column order) and that the sheet ID provided is correct.

6. If you hire/accept this skill from an unknown source, inspect and run the workflows locally in n8n or review the JS nodes carefully — they are readable but any future edits could introduce new behavior. If the author or source is untrusted, prefer implementing equivalent flows yourself or using a vetted marketplace integration.

If you want, I can show a short code snippet to add proper Shopify webhook HMAC verification for the Parse Order node or produce a checklist you can follow before enabling these workflows in production.
